notes_list.title: Reactions Giving Syn Addition
notes_list.basic_overview: Hydroboration and catalytic hydrogenation commonly involve syn addition of the two newly introduced atoms or groups across a pi bond.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Hydroboration–oxidation: H and OH have an overall syn relationship in the appropriate stereochemical description. Lindlar reduction: H2 adds syn to an alkyne to give a cis-alkene.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Hydroboration and catalytic hydrogenation commonly involve syn addition of the two newly introduced atoms or groups across a pi bond. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
